name: Elijah
overview: Elijah was a male prophet known as the Tishbite, one of the settlers of Gilead. He is recognized for his bold prophetic ministry during a critical period in Israel's history. No additional personal notes or tribal affiliations are recorded beyond these details.
namesAndTitles: The name Elijah means 'y-h-v-h is G-d,' reflecting a direct declaration of God's sovereignty. He is also referred to by the title 'man of G-d,' indicating his role as a divine messenger and servant. Both names emphasize his close association with God and his prophetic authority.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Elijah beyond what is listed in his unique attribute as a Tishbite from Gilead. There are no additional familial connections noted in the biblical record.
scriptureSignificance: Elijah is a pivotal figure who confronted idolatry during Israel's apostasy under King Ahab and Queen Jezebel. His ministry included dramatic acts such as calling down fire from heaven and pronouncing drought, demonstrating God's power over false gods. He experienced divine provision and encountered God in a still small voice, highlighting God's presence beyond spectacular displays. Elijah's departure to heaven without dying and his future prophetic role underscore his lasting importance in God's redemptive plan.
